note: What survives the method vocabulary in the core package odoo/, one entry per name with the reason it is not a violation. The core sweep established that this is a list and not a package boundary; the assemble-verb sweep kept it one. There is no --update: an entry is argued, never banked. A name here must be reachable by the gate -- an entry no definition answers to is dead weight, and test_naming_core_vocabulary asserts none is.

names.fetch: reserved -- the ORM read operation that loads stored values into the cache (§2.4.3)
names._fetch_field: reserved -- fetch()'s internals are one contract with it, renamed together or not at all
names._fetch_query: reserved -- as _fetch_field; _get_query would promise a Query return
names.append_paths: reserved -- both halves of the _append_ reservation hold: an ordered list, and an addition at its end, beside an insert_paths that takes the index
names.ensure_db_endpoint: noun -- ensure_db is the route flag declared in addons/web, not a verb
names.remove_control_characters: noun -- a control character is a character
names._read_group_fill_temporal: noun -- fill_temporal is a read_group parameter and a context key
names._check_on_delete_required_m2o: noun -- on_delete is a field on ir.model.fields
names.populate_field: domain verb -- odoo-bin populate is a subcommand whose whole object is populating a database, so §2.4.9's 'where the operation is what the model is about' holds: there is nothing more specific to say than populate
names._populate_models_named: domain verb -- as populate_field; it is the cli/populate.py entry point for the same subcommand
names.invalidate_addon_scan_cache: noun -- the addon scan is the cached thing (_esbuild_addon_scan_cache), not an act this method performs; §2.4.4's 'unless it is a noun', and _invalidate_ is already §2.4.17's canonical
names._check_access: reserved -- `check_access` is the ORM access operation and this is its overridable half: the public one raises, and this returns the raise's material to it (the forbidden records and the error factory). Renaming half a pair splits one contract
names._check_company_domain: protocol -- the check_company mechanism resolves this name on the comodel, exactly as a search hook's contract is a domain (§2.4.1's _search_* exemption). It returns a Domain and would otherwise be _get_domain_*; it is declared on 400+ models across four repositories and a core-only gate must not force that rename
names.check_company_domain_parent_of: protocol -- a canned implementation of _check_company_domain, assigned to it by name on dozens of models. Renaming it without the hook hides the pairing, which is the only thing that says what it is for
names.check_companies_domain_parent_of: protocol -- as check_company_domain_parent_of, for the company_ids side
names.check_values: raises, one frame down -- the failure path is _check_module's raise and the return is the argument passed straight back for chaining. The gate's proxy is one frame deep and this is what it costs
names._check_hostname_callback: raises, one frame down -- match_hostname raises on a certificate that does not match; the bool is pyOpenSSL's verify-callback contract, not an answer this method invented
names.batch_cache_fill: cross-language binding with NO error path -- crates/odoo_rust/src/cache.rs exports the same symbol and libs/accel.py picks between them BY NAME through _pick(), so renaming the Python half does not fail, it silently stops accelerating and the pure-Python twin takes over. Three surface tests pin the name on both sides. The rename is real (noun-first, `fill` in the tail, Mutation row) and needs the Rust source plus a maturin rebuild of the shared venv, so it is a decision rather than a sweep
names.get_hsl_from_seed: noun -- the seed is the string that gets hashed into a hue, and it is this function's parameter name; §2.4.4's 'unless it is a noun' in the trailing position
names._optimize_comodel_id_lookup: noun -- `comodel id lookup` names the DOMAIN SHAPE being optimized (a condition whose subdomain matches on the comodel's id), not an act this function performs; it rewrites that shape and looks nothing up
names._tag_delete: protocol -- tools/convert.py dispatches on `_tag_<xml tag>`, so the tail is the name of the `<delete>` element and not a verb anybody chose; see _tag_record, _tag_menuitem, _tag_asset and the dict that maps 'record' to _tag_record
names._get_databases_to_sweep: noun -- `sweep` is service/_cron.py's own word for one pass of a cron loop over the databases, not §2.4.3's Removal verb: the module exports drain_swept_database beside it and its module docstring says a loop 'waits for a notify before sweeping anyway'. The wrapper is also load-bearing and must not be inlined -- it exists so the seam is a MODULE ATTRIBUTE looked up per call, and test_cron_schedule's test_one_seam_now_reaches_both_loops fails with 'the schedule bound the function instead of the module' the moment a caller binds get_cron_databases directly
names._resolve_webhook_candidates: name resolution -- `resolve` here is the OTHER sense of the word: turn a symbolic reference into the thing it names, total and raising on failure, which §2.4.3 does not print and which is a term of art from a layer below on exactly the terms `reap` and `probe` are. DNS: the body's own diagnostics say 'could not be resolved' and 'resolved to no address'
names._resolve_path_def: name resolution -- `resolve` here is the OTHER sense of the word: turn a symbolic reference into the thing it names, total and raising on failure, which §2.4.3 does not print and which is a term of art from a layer below on exactly the terms `reap` and `probe` are. the asset subsystem's own vocabulary -- it takes a `Resolution`, returns `ResolvedPath`s, and ir_asset.py uses the stem eleven times
names.resolve_reference: name resolution -- `resolve` here is the OTHER sense of the word: turn a symbolic reference into the thing it names, total and raising on failure, which §2.4.3 does not print and which is a term of art from a layer below on exactly the terms `reap` and `probe` are. XML-DSig: `<Reference URI=...>` resolution is the specification's word for this exact operation
names.resolve_mro: name resolution -- `resolve` here is the OTHER sense of the word: turn a symbolic reference into the thing it names, total and raising on failure, which §2.4.3 does not print and which is a term of art from a layer below on exactly the terms `reap` and `probe` are. Python's own: method resolution order
names.resolve_depends: name resolution -- `resolve` here is the OTHER sense of the word: turn a symbolic reference into the thing it names, total and raising on failure, which §2.4.3 does not print and which is a term of art from a layer below on exactly the terms `reap` and `probe` are. turns each dotted @depends path into the Field tuple it names, and raises ValueError on a path that names nothing
names._resolve_runner: name resolution -- `resolve` here is the OTHER sense of the word: turn a symbolic reference into the thing it names, total and raising on failure, which §2.4.3 does not print and which is a term of art from a layer below on exactly the terms `reap` and `probe` are. turns ir.actions.server's `state` into the `_run_action_<state>` method it names, through getattr
names._resolve_render_template: name resolution -- `resolve` here is the OTHER sense of the word: turn a symbolic reference into the thing it names, total and raising on failure, which §2.4.3 does not print and which is a term of art from a layer below on exactly the terms `reap` and `probe` are. turns a template method NAME into the compiled function registered under it
names._resolve_recompute_fields: name resolution -- `resolve` here is the OTHER sense of the word: turn a symbolic reference into the thing it names, total and raising on failure, which §2.4.3 does not print and which is a term of art from a layer below on exactly the terms `reap` and `probe` are. turns field names into the Field objects they name

scopes_note: What survives the vocabulary in a bundled addon, keyed by the --addon scope that reports it. Separate from `names` because an allowlist keyed on the bare name is a claim that the name is unique across every scope, and §2.4.20 records two definitions of _check_path in one tree to say it is not. Same terms as `names`: no --update, an entry is argued.

stock.get_main_lines: stock.traceability.report.get_main_lines is @api.model and is called over RPC by stock_traceability_report_backend.js. It get-or-creates the caller's own report row and returns that row's LINES -- §2.4.11's _get_or_create_ names a producer whose return IS the record it created, and this one's is not: the record is a per-user scratch singleton and the return is the report. The prefix describes the return correctly, which is what the rule tests; renaming it would move an RPC name in two JS files to make a Python reading no more honest.

web.ensure_db: `ensure` is the Validation row's abolished spelling, and this is not a verb in that position: `ensure-db` is a NAMED CONCEPT in odoo/http, declared as ENSURE_DB_PATHS and reached through register_ensure_db_paths() and is_ensure_db_path(), which application.py consults before dispatch. §2.4.3's own test -- ask whether the verb appears as a NOUN in the same scope before collapsing it -- is satisfied by four bindings in the layer below, and §2.4.13 already records this name as one of the four infix hits that are nouns wearing a verb's spelling. It also does not do what _check_ promises: it never raises, it redirects, which is the route-flag behaviour the concept names. Renaming it would rename the concept in odoo/http and in test_http's route, to make a Python reading no more honest.

mail.resolve_data_request: Not a producer at all, which is what the resolve-total rule assumes it is reading. Store.resolve_data_request is a chainable mutator in the Store's own idiom -- add_model_values, delete and bus_send all return Self -- and `resolve` here is the JS PROMISE sense, not §2.4.3's partial producer: it settles the pending data request the client is waiting on. It is also a §2.4.14 binding. The method's whole body sets `_resolve: True` on a DataResponse, and static/src/core/common/data_response_model.js reads that exact key to resolve the promise, so the Python name and the wire key are one word in two languages. Renaming the Python half alone leaves the two spelling the same act differently, which is the cost §2.4.3 weighs when it says a reserved verb frozen into a wire name is a reason to look rather than a reason to keep -- here the look ends in keeping it.
